info.title: OpenPelletBridge REST API
info.description:
REST API running on an ESP32 that talks to Micronova based pellet stoves over the stove serial bus (UART2).

All write parameters are passed as **query parameters** (or `application/x-www-form-urlencoded` form fields), except the timer endpoints which take a **JSON body**.

Most read endpoints query the stove directly over the serial bus; `/api/state` and `/metrics` are served from a cache that a background task refreshes continuously.

**API key (optional).** A random key is generated on first boot. When it is set to required (`POST /api/auth?required=true`), every route except `/`, `/app`, `/api`, `/api-specs.json` and `/api/auth` needs the header `X-API-Key: <key>` or `Authorization: Bearer <key>`; otherwise the response is `401`. Use the **Authorize** button to try the API with a key.

get.description: Served from the sensor cache (no extra serial traffic). `previousErrors` is `false` when the error memory is empty, otherwise an object containing only the non-empty memory positions. `hydro` is only present when hydro mode is enabled in `/config.txt`. get.summary: Log of stove state changes and errors
get.description: Every change of the stove state and of the active error (both read ~1 s), with the exact time. The stove does not store when an error happened; this log is the only source for that. The last 200 entries are kept and persisted to SPIFFS. Recorded once NTP time is available. Oldest first. Errors are only logged once they last 30 s (3 minutes in the transitional states 1, 2, 3, 5, 6) or the stove is in an alarm state. Switchovers of the board's power source (stove supply / USB, OpenPelletBridge board only) are logged as type power. Changes of the pellet reserve sensor (RAM 0xA4) are logged as type pellet; the reserve countdown (RAM 0x89) is not logged (it changes every minute during the reserve; older firmware did, those entries are dropped at the next start).

parameters.name: hours
parameters.description: Only return changes from the last N hours (default: all)

from.description: state: previous stove state code, null for the first logged change; source: stove / remote; power: stove / usb

to.description: state: new stove state code; source: stove / remote; power: stove / usb

up.description: link: true = the stove answers again, false = serial link lost

room.description: source: room temperature at the change

id.description: error: raw error value, 0 = error cleared

error.description: error: error code such as E9, null when cleared

register.description: pellet: RAM register that changed (0xA4 reserve sensor; 0x89 only from older firmware); from/to are its old and new value

post.summary: Firmware update over HTTP
post.description: Streams a firmware image (multipart field `firmware`) to the OTA partition and restarts the controller on success. Always needs the API key (X-API-Key or Authorization: Bearer), also when it is not required for other routes. The fixed OTA password (X-OTA-Password) of older firmware is gone. An image for the other chip or a factory image is refused before anything is written (500).

get.summary: Stove values as one line of numbers (Loxone Virtual HTTP Input)
get.description: One plain text line: `opb seq=1834 state=7 power=1 burn=0 link=1 ... kg=9.5 hAvg=28.5 resMin=-1`. Numbers only: true / false are 1 / 0, unknown is -1. No key ends with another key, so a Loxone command recognition such as `errId=\v` or `kg=\v` is unambiguous. No timestamps: time left instead (alarmMin). `seq` goes up at every change of an event value and at least every heartbeat (interval in /api/loxone/config): Loxone can raise an alarm when it stops changing. Keys: seq, state, power, burn, link, age, errId (0 none, -1 LINK, -2 PELLETS), pendId, pendSec, memErr, warn, wRemote, room, setp, fume, tStove, tRemote, flame, flameAct, fan, fanRun, esOn, esStop, esStart, auger, kg, hNow, hAvg, alarmMin, kgToday, kgDay, eurMonth, bags, lowPel, resMin, resOff, offMin, brzMin, svcH, runH, starts, rssi.

text/plain.example: opb seq=12 state=4 power=1 burn=1 link=1 age=0 errId=0 pendId=0 pendSec=-1 memErr=0 warn=0 wRemote=0 room=20.5 setp=20 fume=74 tStove=21.0 tRemote=16.0 flame=3 flameAct=3 fan=1 fanRun=1 esOn=1 esStop=2 esStart=1 auger=38 kg=9.2 hNow=8.2 hAvg=27.2 alarmMin=1633 kgToday=2.6 kgDay=7.6 eurMonth=84 bags=11.0 lowPel=0 resMin=-1 resOff=0 brzMin=37 svcH=312 runH=5712 starts=1338 rssi=-70

post.summary: Change the Loxone push settings
post.description: Only the given parameters change; stored in NVS, used at once. With push on, the controller sets virtual inputs of the Miniserver itself: `GET http://<host>:<port>/jdev/sps/io/<input>/<value>` with Basic auth. Event values go at once, slow values (temperatures, kg, hours) at most every 60 s after a real difference, all again every 5 min; every answer is checked (HTTP 200 and the code in the LL answer). The switch follows powered on (On / Off, stable for 5 s). Commands from Loxone with the header `X-Source: loxone` (POST /api/power, /api/fan, /api/flame, /api/setpoint, /api/energysaving) are not pushed back; a refused or failed switch-on (409, 500) pushes the real state at once. Basic auth over plain HTTP can be read on the network: use a Loxone user with few rights.

get.description: Running version and the latest GitHub release of netdata-be/PalletHeater-REST-API. Checked automatically when autoCheck is on: right at start-up, before HTTPS reserves its buffers; daily only while HTTPS is off (the check needs the memory of the HTTPS buffers, and the heap could be too fragmented afterwards to reserve them again). Never installs on its own.

post.summary: Check for or install a firmware release
post.description: action=check looks up the latest release; action=install downloads openpelletbridge-firmware.bin over HTTPS, verifies and activates it and restarts the controller (unreachable for about a minute). Both run in the background: poll GET for state and progress. The stove is not affected.

get.summary: Core dump of the last crash
get.description: After a crash (panic, task watchdog) the ESP-IDF stores a core dump (64 KB partition). The summary is also logged at the next start. With download=true the raw dump: decode it with `esp-coredump info_corefile -t raw -c coredump.bin firmware.elf`, using firmware.elf of the same build (CI artifact openpelletbridge-elf-<version>). The backtrace alone: `xtensa-esp32-elf-addr2line -pfiaC -e firmware.elf <addresses>`.

actual.description: Speed the fan really runs at: 0 when stopped, 1-3 derived from the drive value; null when unknown

hotEnough.description: Stove hot enough for the room fan (RAM 0x04); the fan waits for this after ignition

drive.description: Raw power (RAM 0x0A): 0 off; depends on speed and actual flame power, e.g. 9/14/19 at flame 1 and 21/23/25 at flame 2 for speed 1/2/3 (P220 M)

mode.description: From the fan power (RAM 0x0A): off (0) or on

serialNumber.description: Serial number of the stove (MATR on the nameplate), EEPROM 0xCD - 0xCF; null until read

augerPercent.description: Share of the time the auger runs, 0 - 100 % (augerSpeed / 12 s cycle, 100 while pre-loading)

augerSpeed.description: Auger on-time per cycle in seconds (RAM 0x0D / 10; fixed cycle of about 12 s). Named augerSpeed for compatibility.

RemoteControlLastSeen.description: Seconds since last contact with the remote control, -1 if unknown

dataAge.description: Seconds since the cache was last refreshed; null until the first refresh

linkUp.description: false: the stove does not answer, bus commands fail at once

writesUnchanged.description: EEPROM writes left out: the register already held the value

currentError.description: Active error (RAM 0x33): false or the error entry

pelletReserve.description: PELLET RESERVE (installer menu). Seen on this stove: sensor low -> 20 min countdown (counter) -> PELLET RESERVE on the remote, 30 min at flame power 1 (shutdownMinutes) -> the stove switches itself off (switchedOff, error PELLETS).

sensor.description: RAM 0xA4: 0 = enough pellets, 5 = low; 4 seen briefly during a reserve (counts as low)

counter.description: RAM 0x89: minutes of the 20 min countdown after the sensor reports low pellets; alarm at <= 1

minutesLeft.description: Minutes until the reserve alarm while the sensor reports low pellets (RAM 0x89)

shutdownMinutes.description: After the countdown: minutes until the stove switches itself off (RAM 0x91 / 2); the stove runs at flame power 1 meanwhile

switchedOff.description: true once the stove switched itself off because the pellet reserve ran out

refilling.description: RAM 0xA4 counts down 3 -> 0 after a refill: the stove confirms the pellets (one step about every 37 s while burning). shutdownMinutes is null and lowPalletAlarm false meanwhile; switchedOff and the PELLETS error stay until the sensor is 0.

refillConfirmSeconds.description: Estimated seconds until the stove has confirmed the refill (sensor x 37 s); null when no refill is being confirmed

brazierCleaning.description: Brazier cleaning while the stove is working (verified 16/11/2026).

minutesLeft.description: RAM 0x32: minutes to the next brazier cleaning. null when the stove is not working (state 4)

interval.description: EEPROM 0x02: interval between cleanings in minutes

controller.description: Controller (ESP32) firmware build, generated by scripts/buildinfo.py

board.description: Hardware the firmware is built for: ESP32 DevKit or the OpenPelletBridge board (ESP32-S3)

hwRev.description: Hardware revision of the board; not present on the DevKit

features.description: What this build and board have (board.h BOARD_HAS_* flags). bluetooth: BLE built in; onboardLed: the DevKit's plain LEDs; ws2812: RGB status LEDs; buzzer; powerSense: power source sensing (see power); chipTemp: internal temperature sensor (see chipTemp). Clients hide what is not listed; new names may be added.

chipTemp.description: Only with the chipTemp feature (OpenPelletBridge board): internal temperature of the ESP32-S3 in °C, read every 30 s and smoothed; null until the first reading. Warning CHIP_TEMP_HIGH from 70 °C (cleared below 65 °C).

resetReason.description: ESP32 reset reason, plus the cause of a restart the firmware did itself, or after a crash / watchdog reset where the loop task was (and for the task watchdog: for how long, and the task running on each CPU)
resetReason.example: software restart – firmware update from GitHub

crashCount.description: Starts after a crash, watchdog or brown-out

power.description: Only on a board with the powerSense feature (OpenPelletBridge board): where the board takes its power from (TPS2116 power mux: the stove's 5 V first, USB below ~4.3 V). A switchover is logged in /api/events (type power).

source.description: stove: the stove's supply (JP1 / JP2 closed); usb: USB-C

since.description: Unix time (UTC) of the switch to this source, or of the start of the controller if there was none; null without a valid clock (NTP)

calibrated.description: At least one full cycle (refill at the alarm, next alarm) was measured

cycles.description: Measured cycles used for the calibration (last 10)

low.description: Between a low pellet alarm and the refill

remainingKg.description: Pellets left above the level of the low pellet alarm (kg); null = not known yet

hoursLeft.description: Burning hours until the alarm at the current auger value; null while the auger does not feed or not known

hoursLeftAverage.description: Hours until the alarm at the average use of the last 7 days

alarmExpectedAt.description: Expected time of the low pellet alarm at the average use (Unix time)

kgPerHour.description: Consumption at the current auger value

refillKg.description: Amount of an automatically detected refill

lastRefillAt.description: Time of the last refill (Unix time): detected when the low pellet alarm cleared, or entered with add

pendingError.description: Error the stove reports right now (RAM 0x33), also before it counts as currentError, with the seconds until the stove acts on it (RAM 0x30, 55 s for E1 hopper lid open). null without an error.

warnings.description: Warnings while the stove works (not errors). REMOTE_SENSOR_NOT_USED: wireless sensor on, but the stove regulates on its own sensor (remote control not heard). CHIP_TEMP_HIGH (OpenPelletBridge board): the controller chip is at 70 °C or more (controller.chipTemp).

overflow.description: true when more than 600 changes occurred (the rest was dropped)

clientId.description: MQTT client id, also the Home Assistant device id

langActive.description: The language of the texts now

retries.description: Extra attempts after a passing failure (up to 5 attempts per push)

roams.description: Moves to a stronger access point with the same name since the start (the firmware scans while the signal is below -70 dBm and reconnects when another one is 8 dB stronger)

lastRoam.description: Last roam: old -> new access point with signal and channel

country.description: WiFi country code (OPB_WIFI_COUNTRY, default BE, with 802.11d)

saved.description: Settings in NVS, used at the next boot

confirmSecondsLeft.description: Only while a new static IP waits for confirmation

lastChange.description: Outcome of the last network change

switching.description: Only in the response to a network change

accessPoints.description: Every access point of the network the controller is on

devBuild.description: Not exactly a release tag (commits after it, uncommitted changes or no tag)

assetAvailable.description: The release has the image of this board

asset.description: Asset chosen from the latest release (openpelletbridge-firmware.bin, opb-s3: openpelletbridge-opb-s3-firmware.bin); null: none for this board

install.description: What installing the latest release would do

ahead.description: Commits after the release tag (git describe)

lastAttempt.description: Last step of a GitHub install that did not finish (controller restarted or powered off during it) or failed ("failed: ..."), with free heap, largest block, WiFi signal and uptime at that moment. Kept in NVS, so it survives a power cut; removed when an install succeeds.

freeHeap.description: Free heap now (bytes). HTTPS needs about 45 KB

largestBlock.description: Largest free heap block now (bytes). HTTPS needs about 20 KB

trial.description: The running firmware is on trial after an update: confirmed after 2 minutes with WiFi; a restart before that rolls back to the previous firmware

trialSecondsLeft.description: Seconds until the trial ends (with WiFi); null when not on trial

rolledBack.description: Version of the last update that did not start properly and was rolled back; null if none

bootInstall.description: Only from the minimal server during the download after the restart of an install from GitHub (the regular web server is not running then)

phase.description: Step of the download after the restart (with bootInstall)

Pellets.description: Pellet consumption, measured between low pellet alarms. The controller counts auger units (auger value RAM 0x0D x seconds). The level sensor (RAM 0xA4) trips at the same level each time, so between two trips exactly the pellets added in between were burned: kg per unit = kg added / units. A refill is detected when the sensor clears again after a trip (refillKg); topping up without an alarm is entered with add. Cycles are weighted: the newest counts 1, each older one 0.75 times the next.

calibrated.description: At least one full cycle (refill at the alarm, next alarm) was measured

cycles.description: Measured cycles used for the calibration (last 10)

low.description: Between a low pellet alarm and the refill

overdue.description: Burning past the estimate: the counter says the pellets above the sensor are used up, but the alarm did not come yet (remainingKg stays 0). The alarm corrects the calibration.

remainingKg.description: Pellets left above the level of the low pellet alarm (kg); null = not known yet

hoursLeft.description: Burning hours until the alarm at the current auger value; null while the auger does not feed or not known

hoursLeftAverage.description: Hours until the alarm at the average use of the last 7 days

alarmExpectedAt.description: Expected time of the low pellet alarm at the average use (Unix time)

kgPerHour.description: Consumption at the current auger value

refillKg.description: Amount of an automatically detected refill

kgRefilledSinceAlarm.description: kg poured in since the last low pellet alarm (the refills of this cycle); null before the first alarm. Was kgSinceAlarm up to v2.0.0

kgBurnedSinceAlarm.description: kg burned since the last low pellet alarm: auger units since the alarm x kg per unit; null before the first alarm or without calibration

spread.description: Relative standard deviation of the cycles (0.05 = 5 %), from 2 cycles

averageAuger.description: Average auger value over the hourly history of the last 7 days

pendingKg.description: Amount entered while low, used for the refill when the sensor clears

weight.description: Weight of this cycle in kg per unit (newest = 1)

predKg.description: kg the estimate still predicted when this alarm came: > 0 the alarm came early, < 0 late; null = no estimate yet (first cycle)

lastRefillAt.description: Time of the last refill (Unix time): detected when the low pellet alarm cleared, or entered with add

debug.description: GET /api/pellets only: every input and intermediate step of the estimate (input, tracker, constants, calc, loop, save), for troubleshooting. See docs/api.md.

kgToday.description: Pellets burned today (local day), kg; null while not calibrated

kgPerDay.description: Average kg per day over the last 7 days; null while not calibrated

costPerMonth.description: Estimated € per month: kg per day (7 d) x 30.44 x price per kg; null without price or calibration

stockBags.description: Bags in stock; null when not kept

usage.description: GET /api/pellets only: price, stock and use over the last 7 / 30 / 365 days (pricePerBag, bagKg, pricePerKg, stockBags, days, unitsToday, last7, last30, last365 {days, kg, kgPerDay, cost}, stockDays). See docs/api.md.
